claude.sample_unit: test CT scans (each with 4 independent human segmentations)

links.outcome: Fraction of predictions reaching human-level performance after human revision of flagged outlier cases
links.effect: Revision of the top 5% uncertainty-flagged cases (6 cases) raised FT to 0.99 for DSC and NSD, with 1.54 min/case vs 35.4 min manual (23x workload reduction).
links.quote: Overall, this was translated into an FT of 0.99 for both metrics ( Figure 5C ).

links.outcome: Segmentation accuracy versus multi-reader human reference standard, including tail-case failures
links.effect: Best model DSC 0.88 ± 0.04 approached humans, but 3%-5% of cases (best model) and 7%-10% (benchmark) fell below human thresholds vs 1% for humans.
links.quote: Figure 2C-D confirm this trend—human readers had fewer low DSC and NSD cases (1%) compared to AI models (7%–10% for the benchmark, 3%–5% for the best model).

links.outcome: Robustness on held-out test set of older patients differing from training population
links.effect: Failures occurred in cases with fatty infiltration or uncommon anatomy absent from training data; 5%-7% of predictions fell below minimum human performance despite good mean Dice.
links.quote: Our multireader evaluation revealed that even the best-performing pancreas segmentation models lacked robustness: 5% to 7% of predictions fell below the minimum performance threshold in cases that human readers handled consistently.

links.outcome: Uncertainty-based triage identifying cases to defer to humans for revision
links.effect: Acquisition function (entropy + sphericity) inversely correlated with DSC/NSD; revising 6% of cases reduced error rate (1 – FT) to ~1%.
links.quote: Instead, an active learning approach proved effective in this case, reducing the error rate (1 – FT) to ∼1% with manual revision of only 6% of cases, leading to a 23-fold workload reduction.

unlisted_practices: Fractional Threshold robustness metric benchmarking AI against multi-reader human performance distribution
Active learning uncertainty-based selection of outputs for human revision

links.effect: Even best models lacked robustness: 5% to 7% of predictions fell below minimum performance threshold despite high mean metrics.
links.quote: Our multireader evaluation revealed that even the best-performing pancreas segmentation models lacked robustness: 5% to 7% of predictions fell below the minimum performance threshold in cases that human readers handled consistently.

links.effect: Annular pancreas case 79 and duodenal diverticulum case 53 led to segmentation inconsistencies; other errors involved fatty infiltration and low BMI.
links.quote: Additionally, rare anatomical variations, such as annular pancreas (case 79) and duodenal diverticulum (case 53), led to segmentation inconsistencies, likely because of their limited representation in training data.

links.effect: Human revision of the highest-α 6% of test cases made all metrics comparable to humans and yielded FT 0.99 for both metrics.
links.quote: Thus, after human revision of only 6% of the test cases, the model performance in all metrics of interest was comparable to that in humans.

links.effect: High α was inversely correlated with DSC/NSD; 95th-percentile high-α cases were more likely to underperform and were triaged for revision.
links.quote: Figure 5A shows an inverse correlation between the acquisition function α and the DSC/NSD, confirming that cases with high α were more likely to underperform manual segmentation.

links.effect: Low DSC/NSD cases were 1% for humans versus 7%–10% for benchmark AI and 3%–5% for best AI.
links.quote: Figure 2C-D confirm this trend—human readers had fewer low DSC and NSD cases (1%) compared to AI models (7%–10% for the benchmark, 3%–5% for the best model).

links.outcome: Fractional Threshold and segmentation workload with active learning triage
links.effect: active learning revision of 6% uncertain cases raised Fractional Threshold to 0.99 with 23-fold workload reduction (1.54 vs 35.4 minutes/case)
links.quote: Instead, an active learning approach proved effective in this case, reducing the error rate (1 – FT) to ∼1% with manual revision of only 6% of cases, leading to a 23-fold workload reduction.

screen.reason: Evaluates an active learning / human-in-the-loop safeguard where uncertainty-flagged outlier segmentation predictions are routed for human clinician revision to achieve human-level reliability.
